Subject: Bristol Engineering Challenge Invitation

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian Precision are proud to sponsor the 2nd Annual Bristol-Oxford Engineering Challenge on Saturday, November 16.  The purpose of this event is to raise money for both universities, and to enjoy the competitive spirit of the third oldest rivalry in UK higher education.  This year's game marks the 107th meeting between Bristol University and Oxford University, and, with a little luck, the Russell Group Championship will be on the line!

Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian Precision are sponsoring the event, but we need your help as participants and fundraisers.  Contributions raised will benefit the general scholarship fund for each university.

The details:
Date:    Saturday, November 16th

Time:    10:00 a.m. - approximately 4 p.m. (Warm up is at 9:30 am)

Location:   Ashton Park (just off Portbury Road, south of the M5)

Food and Drinks:  Cotswold Smokehouse BBQ (FREE - courtesy of Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd)

Eligibility:   Full-time employees and/or their spouses
    (Players must have graduated from Bristol University or Oxford University)

Team Jerseys:  Provided by Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd and Meridian Precision

Format:   7 players with at least 1 female player on the field at all times

Team Size: Recommend 8-10 players per team (no more than 10 per team)
Contact the team captains to sign-up.  (Sign-up now to ensure your place on a team)

Prizes:    Winning team receives 16 tickets to the Bristol/Oxford match in Oxford on Friday, November 22 Winning team also owns the Engineering Cup trophy until next year!

Fundraising Goal  The committee has set a goal of raising £16,000 for each university.  This will require a contribution of £2,000 per team, plus an equal amount from corporate matching funds.

Last year's event featured a last-minute comeback as Meridian Precision Team 1 defeated the Kestrel Aerospace Components Ltd Team 1 for the championship and took home the tickets and the trophy.  This year, expect the Kestrel team (and Meridian Precision) to come in with revenge on their minds!

Thanks to the gracious gift from the Oxford Alumni, who redirected their donations to the Bristol Foundation, we were able to permanently endow scholarships dedicated to the memory of the 12 engineering scholars who died in last year's Severn Bridge incident.  We believe this event is a great tradition for both companies, and we are pleased to be able to raise important funds for both institutions.
</quoted>
